reason: Carving planks seems like a useful start on the press itself.
expectation: I expect a carved wooden component, though its exact role is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Plant fiber and water might make paper, but I’ll start with the press.
Charcoal and water might make ink, which can come later.

effect: The carved planks produced a printing block, which can now be combined with iron.
reaction: The block makes sense as a carved surface for printing.
reason: Combining the block with iron seems like the most direct next step toward the press.
expectation: I expect a more complete printing mechanism, though I’m unsure exactly what the iron adds.

alternatives.reason: Paper may be useful later, but I’ll continue building the press.
Ink may also be needed later.

effect: The iron completed the press as a screw mechanism, and printing a page is now the goal.
reaction: The explanation of how the screw presses the paper makes the construction clearer.
reason: Plant fiber and water seem like a practical start on paper for the page.
expectation: I expect paper or a material used to make it.

alternatives.reason: Charcoal and water likely make ink, which the page may also need.

effect: The fiber and water made pulp, which can now be combined with cloth to continue making paper.
reaction: The intermediate pulp is a sensible step toward paper.
reason: I’ll continue making the paper needed for the page.
expectation: I expect the cloth to help form or dry the pulp into paper, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Ink will likely be needed too, but I’ll finish the paper first.

effect: The pulp and cloth made paper, ready for printing.
reaction: Finishing the paper is satisfying and straightforward.
reason: Charcoal and water likely make the ink needed to print the page.
expectation: I expect ink or an intermediate ink mixture.

alternatives.reason: The paper needs to reach the press, but I expect ink will be needed first.
Paper and planks might make something useful, but its role in printing is less clear.

effect: Charcoal and water produced ink, so both ink and paper are ready for the press.
reaction: The result was straightforward and expected.
reason: I’ll place the ink at the press to prepare for printing.
expectation: I expect the ink to be positioned for use with the printing block; paper may also need to be placed there.

alternatives.reason: Paper also needs to reach the press, but I’ll place the ink first.

effect: The ink is at the press, enabling the paper-and-ink combination there.
reaction: The next printing step is clear.
reason: Combine the paper with the ink at the press to print the page.
expectation: I expect a printed page using the press and its inked block.

effect: The press produced printed pages and completed the chapter’s final goal.
reaction: Seeing the materials come together into pages was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the press was most worthwhile: the explanation of the iron screw made its operation clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the ink was a straightforward preparation rather than an especially interesting decision.

surprise.text: The iron became a screw in the press, clarifying how the block and paper are pressed together.

arbitrary.text: Paper and planks appeared as an option, but its purpose in printing was unclear; I did not try it.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter: the press explanation and the progression from pulp to printed pages were engaging, though some preparations were routine.
